explain.say: In some places, a column of unusually hot rock called a mantle plume rises from deep inside the Earth. Where it nears the surface it melts rock, making a hot spot.

explain.say: The older islands, away from the heat, stop erupting, cool, erode and sink. That is why in Hawaii the Big Island in the south-east is youngest and still active, and islands get older to the north-west.

faq.a: A hot spot is a place where a plume of extra-hot rock rises from deep in the mantle and melts the rock above it, feeding volcanoes. Unlike most volcanoes, hot spots can be in the middle of a plate.

faq.q: Why do volcanic islands form in a line?
faq.a: The hot spot stays in roughly the same place while the plate moves over it. Each island is carried away as a new one forms, leaving a line of islands that get older with distance.
The Big Island of Hawaii, which sits over the hot spot now and has active volcanoes like Kilauea. A new underwater volcano, Kamaʻehuakanaloa, is growing to its south-east.
Mauna Kea rises about 4,200 metres above sea level, but measured from its base on the sea floor it is over 10,000 metres, taller than Everest from base to top.
asks: Is Mauna Kea taller than Everest?

faq.q: Do all volcanic islands come from hot spots?
faq.a: No. Many, like Japan and Indonesia, form where one plate sinks under another. Iceland forms where plates pull apart, helped by a hot spot.

facts: The Big Island of Hawaii is the youngest of the main Hawaiian islands and sits over the hot spot.
Mauna Kea is over 10,000 metres tall measured from its base on the sea floor.
The Pacific plate moves over the Hawaiian hot spot at roughly 7 to 10 centimetres a year.

quiz.say: In a hot spot island chain, which island is youngest?

options.show: The one right over the hot spot
options.say: The one right over the hot spot

quiz.why: New volcanoes form over the hot spot; older islands have been carried away by the moving plate.

wrong.1: The farthest islands formed first, so they are oldest.
wrong.2: Size depends on how much lava erupted and erosion, not just age.
